text:
Morgan Geekie scored 39 goals last season, and this season the Bruins are getting a different player: more passer, fewer goals. He has 21 points in 25 games, but only six goals against 15 assists, after a year that ran 39 to 29 the other way.

The goals are the part to watch, and the chances say they should come. Geekie's own chance creation is actually up, 1.12 expected goals per 60 minutes on his own shots against 0.95 last season, and he has scored 1.8 fewer goals than those chances deserve. Last season was the reverse, and nobody was going to keep shooting like that. Evolving-Hockey's numbers from 2025-26 even had him better on chance quality than on results. His shot is one of the hardest in the league (98 mph, 99th percentile on NHL EDGE).

He had five assists across two games last weekend, including three in the 7-5 win over Washington, but has gone quiet in two straight losses. His ice time has also slipped by almost a minute over the last ten games. It has been a hard week for the family too: ESPN reported his younger brother Conor, with Tampa Bay, is out four to five months after shoulder surgery.
